en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sahadhammika-vagga 78.
The Training Rule on Eavesdropping.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were quarreling with the well-behaved monks.
The well-behaved monks said this:
"Friends, these group-of-six monks are shameless."
“It is not possible to quarrel with these people.
The group-of-six bhikkhus said this:
“Why, friends, do you revile us with the term ‘shameless’?”
“But where were you, friends, when you heard this?
“We were standing eavesdropping on the Venerable Ones.
Those monks who were of few desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“How indeed can the group-of-six monks stand eavesdropping on monks who have become engaged in quarreling, brawling, and falling into disputes?
… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that you stand eavesdropping on monks who have become engaged in quarreling, brawling, and falling into disputes?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, stand eavesdropping on monks who have fallen into quarreling, strife, and dispute?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so forth].
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Whatever monk should stand eavesdropping on monks who have fallen into quarreling, brawling, or dispute, thinking, ‘I will hear what they say,’ doing so for no other reason than that very purpose, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever monk” means:
Whoever is such a one … [as described] … is called a “bhikkhu” … this is the meaning of “bhikkhu” intended in this context.
"Of the bhikkhus" means of other bhikkhus.
"Engaged in brawling, engaged in quarreling, fallen into disputes" means...
Regarding "of those matters arising from legal disputes":

"He stands eavesdropping" means that he goes there thinking, "Having heard this from them, I will accuse, I will remind, I will counter-accuse, I will counter-remind, or I will humiliate them"; there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he stands where he is and listens, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, while walking behind, he walks hurriedly thinking, "I will listen," there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If he stands where he is and listens, there is an offense of expiation.
If he goes ahead and lags behind, thinking, "I will listen," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Wherever he stands and listens, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
When a bhikkhu comes to where one is standing, sitting, or lying down to converse, one must cough or make oneself known; if one does not cough or make oneself known, there is an offense of expiation.
Making this very condition and no other—
there is no other condition for standing eavesdropping— if one stands eavesdropping upon one who is ordained, perceiving them as ordained, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one stands eavesdropping while [the speaker] is fully ordained, but one is in doubt [as to whether they are so], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one stands eavesdropping while [the speaker] is fully ordained, but one perceives them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If one stands eavesdropping on one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not ordained, but one perceives them as ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not ordained, but one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not ordained, and one perceives them as not ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if one goes thinking, "Having heard this, I will desist, I will abstain, I will pacify myself, and I will liberate myself," or if one is insane.
"For one who is a first offender.
The eighth training rule on eavesdropping is finished.
